sheets.character_en: Alice's sister, a female teenager: a fifteen-year-old English young lady of 1862, about 160 cm tall, slender and graceful, holding still. Warm mid-brown hair a shade darker than a child's, parted in the centre, smoothed over the ears and gathered into a low chignon at the nape in a fine dark hairnet; the chignon and hairnet are clearly visible in the back view. Calm, slightly heavy-lidded grey-blue eyes; a longer oval face, a straight nose and straight brows, a composed mouth, a gentle, slightly dreamy look; fair skin kept pale. Quiet, absorbed expression. She holds a small cloth-bound book in one hand.
sheets.prompt_final: Four-panel character reference sheet following the reference layout: three full-body views (front / side / back) left to right, and one large head-and-shoulders close-up filling the right column; the exact same character, outfit and proportions in every panel; plain background. The sheet looks like four production photographs mounted side by side on one board: the image is divided by three thin vertical gaps into three narrow full-height panels on the left and one wide panel on the right. Panel 1: full-body front view, standing naturally, facing the camera. Panel 2: full-body side profile view facing right. Panel 3: full-body back view. Panel 4 (right column): large head-and-shoulders close-up, facing the camera or a slight three-quarter turn, the face sharp and clear. Each full-body view shows the whole figure from the top of the head to the soles of the shoes with clear space above and below, a small patch of floor and a soft contact shadow under the feet; any part cut off by a panel edge makes the sheet invalid. Plain seamless warm light-grey studio backdrop in every panel, soft even light, no scenery. Identity lock: one and the same person in all four panels, with the same face, hair, build and costume; exactly one figure per panel; no duplicated or extra figures. Character: Alice's sister, a female teenager: a fifteen-year-old English young lady of 1862, about 160 cm tall, slender and graceful, holding still. Warm mid-brown hair a shade darker than a child's, parted in the centre, smoothed over the ears and gathered into a low chignon at the nape in a fine dark hairnet; the chignon and hairnet are clearly visible in the back view. Calm, slightly heavy-lidded grey-blue eyes; a longer oval face, a straight nose and straight brows, a composed mouth, a gentle, slightly dreamy look; fair skin kept pale. Quiet, absorbed expression. She holds a small cloth-bound book in one hand. Costume: an 1862 young lady's summer day dress of soft lilac-grey cotton muslin with a faint white sprig, a fitted bodice with a small round white collar and narrow white cuffs, long coat sleeves, a narrow matching belt at the natural waist, the full skirt reaching the ankle over a modest cage crinoline and white petticoats, white cotton stockings and plain black kid ankle boots; bare-headed; light airy muslin, neat and smooth. Style: Photorealistic live-action fantasy film rooted in England in 1862, shot on 35mm film with anamorphic lenses, 16:9 widescreen. Real sets, real locations and real costumed actors in 1862 dress. Wonderland spaces are real built sets and set extensions in an Alphonse Mucha-inspired Art Nouveau design: flowing organic lines, floral and vine ornament, circular halo roundels, mosaic and stained glass, aged pastel-and-gold surfaces with patina and moss; the waking 1862 meadow stays plain period realism. Talking animals and fantastical creatures are photoreal CGI animals with naturalistic anatomy, real fur, feathers, skin and scales, lit by the same light and grounded with real contact shadows. Natural and practical light: sunlight, candlelight and oil lamps, soft haze with volumetric light shafts and soft colour through stained glass. Restrained palette of verdigris teal, slate grey, dusty rose, soft sage and lilac pastels and tarnished-gold accents, warmed by amber sun and candle glow. Fine film grain, gentle halation, soft depth of field, grounded and quietly melancholy. Layout recap (highest priority): four separate photographic panels side by side on one sheet: front, side profile, back, head-and-shoulders close-up; plain studio backdrop; never one single full-bleed picture.
